svg.text: API Smackdown, November 2026: requests per second
“Hello world” GET, identical 25-byte response · load from k6 2.3.0, 10 virtual users for 30 s, 1 warm-up + 3 measured runs each
AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads); server and load tester on the same machine, cores not pinned
Idiomatic
Tuned for speed
Requests per second, median of 3 runs (higher is better)

svg.text: Key numbers
Rust (hand-written epoll) handled the most requests: 185,227 req/s, 2.4× Python (78,501 req/s).
Lowest p95 latency: Rust (hand-written epoll), 51 µs. Highest: Python, 155 µs.
Tuning vs the idiomatic version: Python (Granian) +62%, Go (fasthttp) +15%, .NET (tuned) +12%, Node (Fastify, all cores)
+12%, Rust (tuned build) +1%.
The hand-written ceiling: 185,227 req/s, 1.1× the fastest idiomatic server (Rust, 175,032 req/s).
Node on all cores vs one process: 12% more requests per second. A small gain like this suggests the load tester, not
Node, was the limit.
Some servers varied between runs: Python (Granian) 120.3k–128.5k (6%), Node (one process) 108.4k–113.1k (4%), Node (all
cores) 120.7k–124.6k (3%), Node (Fastify, all cores) 136.9k–141.2k (3%). The others stayed within 3%.
Every run passed. All 36 runs had zero failed requests, and every response had the expected body.
What the tuned versions change
Rust (hand-written epoll): No framework or async runtime: one thread per core, each with its own listening socket and
epoll loop, and the whole response built once a second. Only handles GET; a demonstration of the ceiling, not a web server.
Rust (tuned build): The same axum code, built with link-time optimisation, a single code-generation unit, instructions
for this exact CPU, and the mimalloc memory allocator.
Go (fasthttp): fasthttp instead of net/http: it reuses request and response objects instead of allocating new ones, but is
not compatible with the standard library.
.NET (tuned): The slim builder with no logging or routing, one bare request handler, and the response bytes encoded once
at startup.
Node (Fastify, all cores): Fastify instead of Express, one worker per core. Fastify prepares its routing and responses up
front, so less work happens per request.
Python (Granian): Granian, a Python server written in Rust, calling a bare app through its own RSGI interface instead of
FastAPI on Uvicorn. One worker per core.
